terms.meaning: small saved settings kept by the browser for this app, which survive a page reload
the corner of the parent area where the panel starts

sections.name: File setup, PanelAnchor
sections.title: Imports and corner choices
sections.what: Brings in the React tools and defines the four corners a panel can start from.
sections.why: The panel needs these tools and a fixed set of starting corners.
sections.watch_out: The corner names are fixed text, so new names need matching code.

sections.name: Position
sections.title: Stored position shape and settings
sections.what: Defines the shape of a saved position and the storage key prefix, plus the gap kept from the edge of the area.
sections.why: Keeps the saved position in a known shape with its own key per panel.
sections.watch_out: Changing the storage key prefix makes all saved positions disappear.

sections.name: readPosition
sections.title: Reading a saved position
sections.what: Reads a panel's saved position from browser storage, and returns nothing if it is missing or damaged.
sections.why: Lets a panel reopen where the user left it.
sections.watch_out: Damaged saved data is ignored quietly, so the panel falls back to its default corner.

sections.name: readCollapsed
sections.title: Reading the collapsed state
sections.what: Reads whether a panel was left collapsed, and treats any problem as not collapsed.
sections.why: Keeps a collapsed panel collapsed after a reload.
sections.watch_out: Any read problem silently gives the expanded state.

sections.name: store
sections.title: Saving position and collapsed state
sections.what: Writes a panel's position and collapsed state to browser storage, and ignores any failure.
sections.why: Storage can be unavailable in some browser modes, and the panel should still work.
sections.watch_out: If storage fails, the position is kept only in memory and is lost on reload.

sections.name: FloatingPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up the panel and placing it
sections.what: Keeps the panel's state, keeps it within its parent area, places it in its starting corner on first show, and re-keeps it in view when the window is resized. It shows nothing when the panel is closed.
sections.why: Lets the panel start in a sensible place and stay visible as the window changes.
sections.watch_out: Placement reads the panel's real size, so it must be drawn before it is measured. The checks depend on the parent element's size.

sections.name: FloatingPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Dragging, collapsing and drawing the panel
sections.what: Lets the user drag the header to move the panel, saves the position when the drag ends, toggles the collapsed state, and draws the header with its buttons and the body.
sections.why: This is the user-facing behaviour of the panel.
sections.watch_out: Clicks on buttons, selectors and inputs in the header do not start a drag. Position is only saved when a drag ends, so a closed browser mid-drag may lose the last move.

summary: A panel that floats over the 3D view. The user can drag it, collapse it, or close it, and the app remembers where it was left.
purpose: Lets the viewer move panels out of the way of the 3D scene.
why: Likely reason: the 3D view needs space, so panels should move and be remembered.
how: On first show it places the panel in the chosen corner. Dragging moves it, and the position is kept within the parent area. Collapsing hides the body. The position and collapsed state are saved in browser storage on release.
inputs: An identifier, title, corner anchor, width, offsets, maximum height, an open flag, a close action and the panel contents.
outputs: A draggable panel element. It also writes its position and collapsed state to browser storage.
risks: Saved positions can point off screen after a window resize, though the code clamps them. In private browsing the saved state is lost on reload.
debug: If a panel will not open, check the open flag and the identifier. If its position is wrong after a reload, check browser storage for the key with the panel prefix.
